_about: General dsh-superagent domain terms (~20-25). Owner: supervisor (batch B1). Each batch adds its own extra terms in src/glossary/<batch>.json. Search this file before you add a term. Definitions follow docs/001-domain.md and docs/002-authorization.md, but every citation here points at the CODE, not the docs.

source.short: A stream of events. A Source kind is a reusable plugin; a Source instance is one configured kind, such as one GitHub repository.
source.long: A kind declares its identity, configuration schema and health entries ({{cite src/sources/kind.ts:84-89}}). SourceRegistry holds the stored instances of each installed kind ({{cite src/sources/registry.ts:45}}).

trigger.short: One immutable event a Source produces, such as a GitHub comment or a Feishu message, with the Source's own metadata.
trigger.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:23-39}} defines the shape: every Thread it belongs to, its actor, whether a person wrote it, and whether it addressed the agent.

thread.short: Triggers in time order. At most one Eval runs on a Thread at a time, and a Thread may carry several Tickets.
thread.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:157-182}} is the aggregate: its Subscriptions, its running Eval (evaluating), and its queued Triggers.

channel.short: The write side of a Thread: where a reply, acknowledgement or result goes back to the Source.
channel.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:9}} is the type: a Source, a Thread and an address the Source's own format defines.

policy.short: The versioned rules for who may start work, and each Source's own part of those rules.
policy.long: {{cite src/core/ports.ts:17-27}} is the port the Engine reads: a version, a gate, Mandate revalidation and the accept-mode check.

eval.short: The judgement on a batch of Triggers: a gate layer, then an assessment, ending in a Decision.
eval.long: {{cite src/core/evals.ts:1}} is the part that runs it; {{cite src/core/model.ts:136-154}} is the Evaluation state it tracks on a Thread.

decision.short: The result of an Eval: accept, stop, ignore, reopen or unavailable, with its reasons.
decision.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:190-209}} is the shape, recorded on the Thread by threadKey.

mandate.short: What an accept grants: the strength, scope and Policy version a Ticket's work relies on. It never changes once set.
mandate.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:126-133}} is the shape. Only accept creates one; a person's stop withdraws it; failed revalidation revokes it ({{cite docs/002-authorization.md:129}}).

strength.short: How a Trigger was admitted: explicit, inferred, or not admitted (no Mandate at all).
strength.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:96}} types the two Mandate-bearing values; {{cite src/core/ports.ts:7}}'s GateResult shows the third case as admissible: false, which carries no strength.

accept-mode.short: The Policy setting that controls inferred candidates: off, observe (assess but never accept) or auto (assess and accept).
accept-mode.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:103}} is the type. Policy.admitsInferred ({{cite src/core/ports.ts:24}}) checks it against the matched rules.

ticket.short: A unit of authorized work. Only an Eval's accept creates one; it goes open to ended and sometimes back to open.
ticket.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:277-308}} is the aggregate: its Mandate, Channels, Assignments and Inputs.

stage.short: An open Ticket's current wait: idle, working (plain or queued), or person (delivery, answer, review, blocked or failed).
stage.long: {{cite src/core/stage.ts:4-6}} is the type; {{cite src/core/stage.ts:8-21}}'s ticketStage computes it, row by row, from the Ticket's own stored facts.

assignment.short: The binding of a Ticket to one Executor instance. A Ticket has several over time, one running at a time.
assignment.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:218-233}} is the shape: its state, its latest Report, and when Inputs last reached it.

subscription.short: The many-to-many link between Tickets and Threads. A Trigger on a subscribed Thread reaches every live subscribed Ticket.
subscription.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:163-164}} holds the list on the Thread; {{cite src/core/tickets.ts:417-422}}'s subscribe adds to it, and {{cite src/core/intake.ts:34-48}} fans a Trigger out through it.

effect.short: One durable row in the side-effect queue: a launch, a delivery, a relay, a notice or a reply, run after its transaction commits.
effect.long: {{cite src/app/effects.ts:11-24}} lists the six kinds; {{cite src/app/effects.ts:42-46}} describes the queue itself.

executor.short: The port that runs Assignments: one Executor Session and one directory per Ticket.
executor.long: {{cite src/core/ports.ts:59-69}} is the port the Engine calls; {{cite src/executor/dsh.ts:207}}'s DshExecutor is the only implementation in this repository.

worker-slot.short: One unit of the Executor's concurrency limit. A Ticket holds one while its worker launches, runs a turn, or finishes background work.
worker-slot.long: {{cite src/executor/dsh.ts:171-199}}'s WorkerSlots tracks them, with one extra slot reserved for a person's message.

report.short: What an Assignment reports back to its Ticket: progress, waiting, ready, blocked, failed or dropped.
report.long: {{cite src/core/model.ts:216}} types the states; {{cite src/core/assignments.ts:11-20}}'s WorkerReport is what a worker or the Executor itself sends in.

outbox.short: The Engine's port for Channel writes: it keeps a receipt for every outgoing message and sends it as durable work.
outbox.long: {{cite src/core/ports.ts:76-83}} is the port; {{cite src/app/outbox.ts:22-52}}'s Outbox class is the implementation, backed by a reply Effect.

management-api.short: The local HTTP API the panel uses, and that scripts and agents can also call, under one path prefix.
management-api.long: {{cite src/app/http.ts:230-234}} registers the /orchestrator/api/ prefix with a same-origin check.

dsh-bundle.short: How dsh-superagent ships: a package with a Cordis patch file that a DSH profile loads, not a standalone program.
dsh-bundle.long: {{cite package.json:30-33}} points dsh.bundle.patch at {{cite cordis.patch.yml:4-6}}, which inserts the plugin.

dsh-profile.short: A named DeepSeek Harness configuration and runtime. dsh-superagent runs in its own profile, separate from a person's own.
dsh-profile.long: {{cite scripts/dsh-superagent:2}} names the default profile, superagent; {{cite scripts/dsh-superagent:30-32}} keeps each profile's control files apart.
